key_insight: Jointly pricing compute, memory, and future session reuse enables better routing and KV-cache retention for multi-turn LLM inference.
engineering_relevance: PARK turns this resource-allocation framework into a practical controller that improves GPU serving throughput while preserving reusable prefixes.
method: Derive admission, routing, and eviction rules from a fluid model using resource shadow prices and session continuation values.
Develop an asymptotically optimal buffer-reserve policy for stochastic fluctuations.
Implement online price updates, one-turn migration lookahead, and KV retention ranked by expected reuse value per byte-epoch.
evidence_signal: For a 197B-parameter MoE model on 16 H200 GPUs, PARK improves output throughput over the strongest baseline by 24.2% on SWE and 40.0% on Terminal-Bench; 128-GPU experiments achieve 91.3–97.4% prefix-cache hit rates.
watch_item: Production effectiveness depends on estimating future reuse and resource prices despite asynchronous arrivals and delayed load reports.
paper_title: Routing and Cache Retention for Multi-Turn LLM Inference: Theory and Implementation
